title: Comparative Export Regulations for Ayurvedic Products (US FDA & European Union)
authority: US FDA (21 CFR Part 111) / European Medicines Agency (EMA Directive 2004/24/EC)

jurisdictions.regulatory_pathway: Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA 1994) / 21 CFR Part 111

rules.text: Ayurvedic products are marketed primarily as Dietary Supplements, not as drugs. Must not contain prohibited heavy metals (Lead, Mercury, Arsenic) or undeclared pharmaceutical adulterants.

rules.clause: Structure / Function Claims vs Disease Claims
rules.text: Manufacturers may make Structure/Function claims (e.g. 'Supports joint flexibility', 'Promotes restful sleep') accompanied by the mandatory FDA disclaimer. Disease treatment/cure claims (e.g. 'Cures arthritis') are strictly forbidden and constitute unapproved new drugs.
rules.relevance: Label compliance for exports to USA.

rules.text: Any botanical ingredient not marketed in the US prior to October 15, 1994 requires a 75-day pre-market safety notification under Section 413 of the FD&C Act.

jurisdictions.regulatory_pathway: Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (THMPD - Directive 2004/24/EC)

rules.text: Requires documentary evidence of uninterrupted traditional medicinal use for at least 30 years preceding the application, including at least 15 years within the European Union.
rules.relevance: Major barrier for traditional Ayurvedic polyherbals without prior EU presence; alternative pathway is EU Food Supplement under Directive 2002/46/EC.

rules.text: Strict maximum contaminant thresholds for Lead (<3.0 mg/kg), Cadmium (<1.0 mg/kg), Mercury (<0.1 mg/kg) and total Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids (<1.0 microgram/day).
rules.relevance: Laboratory testing specification for EU export batches.

jurisdictions.regulatory_pathway: CITES Appendix II / Foreign Trade Policy

rules.text: Species listed in CITES Appendix II (e.g. Red Sandalwood Pterocarpus santalinus, Agarwood Aquilaria malaccensis, Kutki Picrorhiza kurroa) require a valid CITES Export Permit issued by the Assistant Management Authority of India (Wildlife Crime Control Bureau) accompanied by Legal Procurement Certificates (LPC).
rules.relevance: Mandatory customs clearance permit for international shipment of protected botanicals.
